etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English, from Middle French fertile, from Old French fertile, from Latin fertilis (“fruitful, fertile”), from ferō (“I bear, carry”).

definitions.definition: Of land, etc.: capable of growing abundant crops; productive.
(figuratively) Of one's imagination, etc.: active, productive, prolific.
Capable of developing past the egg stage.
(physics) Not itself fissile, but able to be converted into a fissile material by irradiation in a reactor.
